The resulting procedures are novel in the sense that they are valid in finite samples when the exposure is marginally independent of the outcome ($\bm Y$) and covariates, and asymptotically valid under the broader conditional independence null, $\bm X\indep \bm Y\mid \bm Z$, subject to method-specific conditions. For generalized linear model scores, separately studentizing the observed and permuted scores yields validity under a correctly specified null mean despite \emph{arbitrary} conditional variance misspecification. Moreover, the permutation calibration also applies to tests based on generalized and projected covariance measures. Their validity accommodates machine learning nuisance estimates under a condition on the stability of refitting after permutation, for which we provide sufficient conditions for common regression learners. Permutation calibration preserves first-order local power while better capturing the finite-sample discreteness and skewness induced by sparse observations. Simulations and single-cell CRISPR screen analysis show substantial calibration gains with our methods when effective sample size is small.
item.dc:creator: Jiahao Ai, Ziang Niu

item.title: Calibrated Multiaccuracy: Deterministic and Randomized Sample Complexity
item.description: arXiv:2611.03305v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Calibrated multiaccuracy asks that a predictor be globally calibrated and multiaccurate with respect to a bounded test family $G$; that is, its residuals should be uncorrelated with every test $g(x)\in G$. This weakening of multicalibration suffices for many applications. Its sample complexity was not known to improve on that of full multicalibration, which is $\widetilde\Theta\left(\frac{\log|G|}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{1}{\varepsilon^{3}}\right)$ when $|G|$ is at least a sufficiently large power of $\log(1/\varepsilon)$. We resolve the sample complexity of $\varepsilon$-calibrated multiaccuracy, showing that it scales as $$ \widetilde\Theta\left(\frac{\log|G|}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{1}{\varepsilon^{5/2}}\right), $$ separating it from the complexity of multicalibration. The upper bound is obtained by an algorithm that outputs a randomized predictor. For deterministic predictors, we establish the tight rate $$ \widetilde\Theta\left( \frac{\log|G|}{\varepsilon^2} + \frac{(\log|G|)^{1/3}}{\varepsilon^{8/3}} \right) $$ whenever $\log|G|=\Omega(\log(1/\varepsilon))$. When $\log|G|\le\varepsilon^{-1+\kappa}$ for any fixed $\kappa\in(0,1)$, this rate is polynomially larger than the rate for randomized predictors. Thus, unlike for multicalibration, calibrated multiaccuracy exhibits a genuine sample-complexity separation between deterministic and randomized predictors. The matching upper and lower bounds show that the unusual cube-root dependence on $\log|G|$ is intrinsic. At $\log|G|\asymp\varepsilon^{-1}$, the minimax rates for randomized and deterministic calibrated multiaccuracy both coincide with the minimax rate for multicalibration.
item.dc:creator: Jiuyao Lu, Georgy Noarov, Aaron Roth

item.title: Subpolynomial-Query Proximal Sampling Beyond Log-Concavity
item.description:
arXiv:2611.03442v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We study the gradient query complexity of sampling from a density $\pi(x)\propto\mathrm{e}^{-V(x)}$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$, where $V$ has a $ eta$-Lipschitz gradient but need not be convex. Our approach uses the proximal sampler, which alternates Gaussian perturbation with sampling a position conditional on the noisy observation. We implement its observation chain using the high-order noisy conditional sampler of [OpenAI 2026], obtaining improved dimension dependence under functional inequalities. If $\pi$ satisfies a log-Sobolev inequality (LSI) with constant $\alpha$, then for every fixed $
u>0$, there is a finite constant $C_
u$ depending only on $
u$ such that the algorithm returns a sample within total-variation distance $\varepsilon$ using at most $C_
u\kappa(d+\kappa+\varepsilon^{-1}+\|
abla V(x_0)\|^2/ eta)^
u$ queries, where $\kappa= eta/\alpha$ and $x_0$ is an arbitrary reference point for initialization. The analysis controls center-dependent local errors along exact proximal histories and removes the final observation noise by conditional decoding. Under a Poincar'e inequality (PI), we obtain a corresponding guarantee from a warm start with a known bound on its R'enyi divergence. An oracle lower bound shows that a stationary point alone, which suffices under LSI, is insufficient under PI.
item.dc:creator: Wei Guo, Bo Yuan, Ye He, Jiaming Liang, Molei Tao, Yongxin Chen

item.title: Theoretical Guarantees for the Subspace-Constrained Tyler's Estimator
item.description: arXiv:2403.18658v5 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the subspace-constrained Tyler's estimator (STE) for recovering a low-dimensional linear subspace from data contaminated by outliers. Under deterministic conditions on inlier spread and outlier alignment, we prove linear convergence to the true subspace from a sufficiently accurate initialization. The guarantee also applies when the dimension-scaled signal-to-noise ratio is below one, where general robust subspace recovery is SSE-hard. When initializing STE from a candidate subspace, we provide a sufficient recovery condition based on the initial angular error and the size of the identity shift applied to the subspace projector. For noisy inliers, we prove a subspace error proportional to the noise level within an explicit iteration bound. Finally, under an asymptotic, anisotropic Gaussian inlier--outlier model, we show that Tyler's M-estimator (TME) provides a successful STE initialization even when TME's own leading eigenspace differs from the target subspace.
item.dc:creator: Gilad Lerman, Teng Zhang

item.title: Private Minimum Hellinger Distance Estimation via Hellinger Distance Differential Privacy
item.description: arXiv:2501.14974v4 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Objective functions based on Hellinger distance yield robust and efficient estimators of model parameters. Motivated by privacy and regulatory requirements encountered in contemporary applications, we derive in this paper \emph{private minimum Hellinger distance estimators}. The estimators satisfy a new privacy constraint, namely, Hellinger differential privacy, while retaining the robustness and efficiency properties. We demonstrate that Hellinger differential privacy shares several features of standard differential privacy while allowing for sharper inference. Additionally, for computational purposes, we also develop Hellinger differentially private gradient descent and Newton-Raphson algorithms. We illustrate the behavior of our estimators in finite samples using numerical experiments and verify that they retain robustness properties under gross-error contamination.
item.dc:creator: Fengnan Deng, Anand N. Vidyashankar

item.title: The Root Finding Problem Revisited: Beyond the Robbins-Monro procedure
item.description: arXiv:2508.17591v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the sequential root-finding problem with repeated noisy measurements. We propose sequential-test bisection STB, which uses a nonparametric sequential sign test to determine when to move to a new design point. Compared with variants of stochastic approximation, STB offers broader adaptivity and faster convergence. When the regression function satisfies $|f(x)|\geq \textsf{c}_0|x-\theta|^\gamma$ in a neighborhood of $\theta$ for constants $\textsf{c}_0,\gamma>0$ where $\theta$ is the root, i.e. $f(\theta) = 0$, we establish non-asymptotic guarantees showing that STB, without using the knowledge of $\gamma$, achieves the minimax adaptive optimal convergence rate $\widetilde{O}(n^{-1/(2\gamma)})$, outperforming Robbins--Monro and related stochastic-approximation methods in convergence rate. Under sub-Gaussian noise, STB provides finite-sample confidence sequences for the root $\theta$ without estimating a derivative. In the positive-slope model, we augment STB with {randomized weighted-section and a line fitted to all observations}, leading to asymptotic normality and consistent variance estimation. We formalize the efficiency by a convolution theorem of H\'ajek-Le Cam type. Furthermore, when the regression function is discontinuous at the root, we show that Robbins--Monro converges at rate $1/n$, whereas STB converges super-polynomially. We extend this construction to multivariate nonparametric level-set estimation by sampling along rays. As a technical byproduct, we establish a new central limit theorem under random stopping, with proof techniques that may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Yue Yu, Moulinath Banerjee, Ya'acov Ritov

item.title: Measuring the roughness of a signal
item.description: arXiv:2610.05457v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We study the non-parametric estimation of the roughness of a path from discretely sampled observations. Our approach is based on the concept of normalized power variation of a path. The estimator identifies a variation index by comparing coarse increments with local sums of fine increments. We prove pathwise consistency under H\"older regularity, nondegenerate coarse critical power sums, uniform local bounds on fine critical power sums, and separation of the two sampling scales and obtain a convergence rate for the estimator. Neither convergence of critical variation nor monotonicity of the finite-sample statistic is required. The result applies to fractional Brownian motion under dyadic sampling and to Schauder series with bounded coefficients bounded away from zero. For signed Takagi--Landsberg functions we obtain a uniform asymptotic formula and a quantitative bound for every root of the estimating equation in a fixed parameter interval. For fractional Brownian motion, we obtain asymptotic uniqueness of the estimating root and a polynomial almost-sure error bound. We illustrate the results with numerical experiments for Takagi-Landsberg functions, fractional Brownian motion and the stochastic heat equation.
item.dc:creator: Rama Cont, Purba Das

item.title: Stationary Unit Roots and Inference in Softplus INGARCH Models
item.description: arXiv:2610.19421v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: A unit root makes linear count time series models such as the Poisson INGARCH(1,1) nonstationary. We show that a softplus link changes this. Wei{\ss}, Zhu and Hoshiyar (2022) introduced softplus INGARCH models and gave a sufficient condition for stationarity. For Poisson, negative binomial, gamma and related versions of these models, we obtain the necessary and sufficient condition, which allows a unit root. At a stationary unit root, the conditional mean has a power-law tail, and the observations can have infinite variance or long memory. To our knowledge, this is the first stationary unit root established for an INGARCH-type count model. For a fixed softplus scale, the Poisson quasi-maximum likelihood estimator is asymptotically normal both below and at the unit root, including cases with infinite variance. Two applications show that unit-root conclusions can depend on the softplus scale.
item.dc:creator: Yang Lu, Fukang Zhu

item.title: Time-Uniform Dependent Central Limit Theory
item.description: arXiv:2610.29288v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We establish a near-optimal almost sure invariance principle for nonstationary time series under the functional dependence measure (FDM) framework. This result yields a universal time-uniform dependent central limit theorem, which serves as the basis for anytime-valid inference. In particular, we instantiate the theorem through asymptotic confidence sequences (AsympCSs), time-uniform counterparts of asymptotic confidence intervals obtained via central limit theorems, extending those originally proposed in Waudby-Smith et al. (2024) to time series with serial dependence. We further refine the original definition because, as we show, it can admit AsympCSs that fail to achieve asymptotic time-uniform coverage even for independent and identically distributed settings. We address this issue by adding a simple eventual-inclusion condition, which in turn permits more flexible variance estimation. In time-series settings, this relaxation can substantially ease restrictions on bandwidth and kernel selection. For feasible implementation of AsympCSs, we establish strong consistency of HAC variance estimators under the FDM framework, accommodating a wider range of commonly used bandwidth choices than existing results under mixing conditions. As illustrations, we construct AsympCSs for algorithms with Markovian structure and time-series-based causal estimands.
item.dc:creator: Mingxuan Ge, Yanlong Liu

item.title: Beyond Brown's radial tests: admissibility, parabolicity, and a doubling-Poincar\'e prior that neither test decides
item.description: arXiv:2610.34309v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For the estimation of a normal mean in $\mathbb{R}^m$ under quadratic loss, Brown (1971) proved that a generalized Bayes estimator $\delta_F$ with bounded drift is admissible if and only if a diffusion attached to the marginal $f^*$ of the prior $F$ is recurrent, and gave two radial tests: a sphere-average test for recurrence and a ray test for transience. He observed that both tests can be silent. We read his theory as the potential theory of the weighted Euclidean space $(\mathbb{R}^m,f^*\,dx)$ and ask what the modern theory of recurrence on weighted manifolds adds inside the zone where neither test applies. Three results. (A) If $f^*\,dx$ is doubling and supports a scale-invariant Poincar\'e inequality, the sphere test is already complete: recurrence, Brown's sphere test and the ball-volume test are equivalent, so geometric criteria can add decidable cases only on the inadmissible side. (B) They do add one. An explicit prior on $\mathbb{R}^3$ whose marginal is small along a lattice of circles at dyadic scales with spacing equal to the square root of the scale, is doubling and Poincar\'e, silences both of Brown's tests, and is transient by the ball-volume test; its generalized Bayes estimator is inadmissible. (C) Outside the doubling-Poincar\'e class the zone is two-sided: the same circles placed on one surface per scale give an admissible estimator, decided by a flux bound along a non-spherical exhaustion, and a logarithmic product prior gives an inadmissible one, decided by product heat kernels. A comparison lemma shows that any positive weight with Lipschitz logarithm is, up to constants, the marginal of a prior, so that explicit weights may be used throughout.
item.dc:creator: Oleg Roshka

item.title: Setting Things Straight: On the Straightness and Non-Straightness of Two-Step Rectified Flow
item.description: arXiv:2610.36090v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Rectified flow (RF) is an ODE-based generative modeling framework that has achieved remarkable success in practice over the past few years. By design, RF seeks to produce flows that have a high degree of straightness, in the sense that the resulting ODE trajectories can be obtained with relatively few (ideally, one) sampling steps. However, a rigorous analysis of straightness or near-straightness of RF flows remains missing in the literature. In this paper, we study settings in which the coupling generated by two-step RF is provably straight at the population level. We provide a complete characterization in two popular classes of data distributions: (i) smooth, strongly log-concave densities and (ii) Gaussian mixture models. Our main results yield sharp conditions for the coupling generated by two-step RF to be straight. Non-straight couplings are constructed when these conditions fail, which demonstrate the sharpness of these conditions. Using the theory developed on the straightness of two-step RF, we propose a notion of approximate straightness that measures the straightness of the learned couplings and can be estimated from the data. We introduce a procedure for constructing asymptotic confidence intervals for our proposed notion of approximate straightness and propose a data-driven method for selecting the number of reflow rounds in multiple iterations of RF.
item.dc:creator: Tuan Pham, Saptarshi Roy, Alessandro Rinaldo, Purnamrita Sarkar

item.title: A Generalized Tangent Approximation based Variational Inference Framework for Strongly Super-Gaussian Likelihoods
item.description: arXiv:2504.05431v5 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Variational inference, as an alternative to Markov chain Monte Carlo sampling, has played a transformative role in enabling scalable computation for complex Bayesian models. Nevertheless, existing approaches often depend on either rigid model-specific formulations or stochastic black-box optimization routines. Tangent approximation is a principled class of structured variational methods that exploit the geometry of the underlying probability model. However, its utility has largely been confined to logistic regression and related modeling regimes. In this article, we propose a novel variational framework based on tangent transformation for a broad class of probability models characterized by strongly super-Gaussian likelihoods. Our method leverages convex duality to construct tangent minorants of the log-likelihood, thereby inducing conjugacy with Gaussian priors over model parameters in an otherwise intractable setup. Under mild assumptions on the data-generating mechanism, we establish algorithmic convergence guarantees, a contribution that stands in contrast to the limited theoretical assurances typically available for black-box variational methods. Additionally, we derive near-parametric variational risk bounds. Superior performance of our proposed methodology is illustrated on simulated and real-data scenarios that challenge state-of-the-art variational algorithms in terms of scalability and their ability to consistently capture complex underlying data structure.
item.dc:creator: Somjit Roy, Pritam Dey, Debdeep Pati, Bani K. Mallick

item.title: Canonical Forms as Dual Volumes
item.description: arXiv:2509.02239v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study dual volume representations of canonical forms for positive geometries in projective spaces, expressing their rational canonical functions as Laplace transforms of measures supported on the convex dual of the semialgebraic set. More generally, for hyperbolic positive geometries the inverse Laplace transform is naturally understood as a distribution supported on the closed dual cone. When this distribution is a non-negative measure, we term the geometry completely monotone, reflecting the property of its canonical function. We identify a class of positive geometries with hyperbolic algebraic boundary for which this cone-supported distribution exists. In particular, simplex-like minimal spectrahedra are completely monotone, with representing measures governed by the Riesz--Wishart theory of the cone of positive semidefinite matrices and admitting integral descriptions over spectrahedral slices and lower-rank strata. We explicitly compute these measures for positive geometries in the projective plane bounded by lines and conics or by a nodal cubic, revealing periods evaluating to transcendental functions. This dual volume perspective replaces logarithmic differential forms by dual measures in the completely monotone case, forging new connections to hyperbolic differential operators, convex optimization and algebraic statistics.
item.dc:creator: Elia Mazzucchelli, Prashanth Raman

item.title: Robust Cauchy-Based Methods for Predictive Regressions
item.description: arXiv:2511.09249v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper develops robust inference methods for predictive regressions that address key challenges posed by endogenously persistent or heavy-tailed regressors, as well as persistent volatility in errors. Building on the Cauchy estimation framework, we propose two novel tests: one based on $t$-statistic group inference and the other employing a hybrid approach that combines Cauchy and OLS estimation. These methods effectively mitigate size distortions that commonly arise in standard inference procedures under endogeneity, near nonstationarity, heavy tails, and persistent volatility. The proposed tests are simple to implement and applicable to both continuous- and discrete-time models. Extensive simulation experiments demonstrate favorable finite-sample performance across a range of realistic settings. An empirical application examines the predictability of excess stock returns using the dividend-price and earnings-price ratios as predictors. The results suggest that the dividend-price ratio possesses predictive power, whereas the earnings-price ratio does not significantly forecast returns.
item.dc:creator: Rustam Ibragimov, Jihyun Kim, Anton Skrobotov

item.title: Measures and Models of Non-Monotonic Dependence
item.description: arXiv:2512.10828v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A margin-free measure of bivariate association generalizing Spearman's rho to the case of non-monotonic dependence is defined in terms of two square integrable functions on the unit interval. Properties of generalized Spearman correlation are investigated when the functions are piecewise continuous and strictly monotonic, with particular focus on the special cases where the functions are drawn from orthonormal bases defined by Legendre polynomials and cosine functions. For continuous random variables, generalized Spearman correlation is treated as a copula-based measure and shown to depend on a pair of uniform-distribution-preserving (udp) transformations determined by the underlying functions. Bounds for generalized Spearman correlation are derived and a novel technique referred to as stochastic inversion of udp transformations is used to construct singular copulas that attain the bounds and parametric copulas with densities that interpolate between the bounds and model different degrees of non-monotonic dependence. Sample analogues of generalized Spearman correlation are proposed and their asymptotic properties are investigated. Potential applications of the theory are demonstrated including: exploratory analyses of the dependence structures of datasets and their symmetries; elicitation of functions maximizing generalized Spearman correlation via expansions in orthonormal basis functions; and construction of tractable probability densities to model a wide variety of non-monotonic dependencies.
item.dc:creator: Alexander J. McNeil, Johanna G. Neslehova, Andrew D. Smith

item.title: Decoupled Kemeny quasi-likelihoods for rank-based generalised linear models
item.description: arXiv:2601.00188v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: This paper introduces a unified profile quasi-likelihood framework for generalised linear models built on a topologically complete extension to Kendall's $\tau$ with finite sample power and Type-I error rates. By establishing equivalence between continuous $L^2$ profile estimators and discrete Generalized Gibbs exponential families, we prove local asymptotic minimax efficiency over the copula tangent space. The framework yields monotone-affine invariant inference, sub-Gaussian concentration bounds, and exact finite-sample $t$-pivot tail majorization under arbitrary tie configurations. We illustrate the methodology through three canonical applications: bivariate rank correlation, paired testing, and intraclass correlation.
item.dc:creator: Landon Hurley

item.title: Inference-Time Alignment for Diffusion Models via Variationally Stable Doob's Matching
item.description: arXiv:2601.06514v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Inference-time alignment for diffusion models aims to adapt a pre-trained reference diffusion model toward a target distribution without retraining the reference score network, thereby preserving the generative capacity of the reference model while enforcing desired properties at inference time. A central mechanism for achieving such alignment is guidance, which modifies the sampling dynamics through an additional drift term. In this work, we introduce variationally stable Doob's matching, a novel framework for provable guidance estimation grounded in Doob's $h$-transform. Our approach formulates guidance as the gradient of the logarithm of an underlying Doob's $h$-function and employs gradient-regularized regression to simultaneously estimate both the $h$-function and its gradient, resulting in a consistent estimator of the guidance. Theoretically, we establish non-asymptotic convergence rates for the estimated guidance. Moreover, we analyze the resulting controllable diffusion processes and prove non-asymptotic convergence guarantees for the generated distributions in the Wasserstein-2 distance. Finally, we show that variationally stable guidance estimators are adaptive to unknown low dimensionality, effectively mitigating the curse of dimensionality under low-dimensional linear subspace assumptions. Numerical experiments demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed method and show the advantages compared to the baselines.
item.dc:creator: Jinyuan Chang, Chenguang Duan, Yuling Jiao, Ruoxuan Li, Yi Xu, Jerry Zhijian Yang

item.title: Finite-sample Valid Permutation Inference under Multi-way Clustering
item.description: arXiv:2601.08610v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Econometric applications with multi-way clustering often feature a small number of effective clusters or heavy-tailed data, making standard cluster-robust and bootstrap inference unreliable in finite samples. In this paper, we develop a framework for finite-sample valid permutation inference in linear regression with multi-way clustering under an assumption of conditional exchangeability of the errors. Our assumption is closely related to the notion of separate exchangeability studied in earlier work, but can be more realistic in many economic settings as it imposes minimal restrictions on the covariate distribution. We construct permutation tests of significance that are valid in finite samples and establish theoretical power guarantees, in contrast to existing methods that are justified only asymptotically. While our main presentation is under exchangeable errors, our framework encompasses invariance-based tests that remain valid under general forms of heteroskedastic errors. We also extend our methodology to settings with missing data and derive power results that reveal phase transitions in detectability. Through simulation studies, we demonstrate that the proposed tests maintain correct size and competitive power, while standard cluster-robust and bootstrap procedures can exhibit substantial size distortions.
item.dc:creator: Wenxuan Guo, Panos Toulis, Yuhao Wang

item.title: Low-Dimensional Adaptation of Rectified Flow: A Diffusion and Stochastic Localization Perspective
item.description: arXiv:2601.15500v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: In recent years, Rectified flow (RF) has gained considerable popularity largely due to its generation efficiency and state-of-the-art performance. In this paper, we investigate how well RF automatically adapts to the intrinsic low dimensionality of the support of the target distribution to accelerate sampling. We show that, using a carefully designed \blue{end-point adapted} time-discretization scheme and with sufficiently accurate drift estimates, the RF sampler enjoys an iteration complexity of order $O(k/\varepsilon)$ (up to log factors), where $\varepsilon$ is the precision in total variation distance and $k$ is the intrinsic dimension of the target distribution. In addition, we show that the denoising diffusion probabilistic model (DDPM) procedure is equivalent to a stochastic version of RF by establishing a novel connection between these processes and stochastic localization. Building on this connection, we further design a stochastic RF sampler that also adapts to the low-dimensionality of the target distribution under mild requirements on the accuracy of the drift estimates, and also with a specific time schedule. We illustrate the efficacy of newly designed time-discretization schedules with simulations on the synthetic data and text-to-image (T2I) data experiments.
item.dc:creator: Saptarshi Roy, Alessandro Rinaldo, Purnamrita Sarkar

item.title: Zero Variance Portfolio
item.description: arXiv:2602.19462v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: When the number of assets is larger than the sample size, the minimum variance portfolio interpolates the training data, delivering pathological zero in-sample variance. We show that if the weights of the zero variance portfolio are learned by a novel ``Ridgelet'' estimator, in a new test data this portfolio enjoys out-of-sample generalizability. It exhibits the double descent phenomenon and can achieve optimal risk in the overparametrized regime when the number of assets dominates the sample size. In contrast, a ``Ridgeless'' estimator which invokes the pseudoinverse fails in-sample interpolation and diverges away from out-of-sample optimality. Extensive simulations and empirical studies demonstrate that the Ridgelet method performs competitively in high-dimensional portfolio optimization.
item.dc:creator: Jinyuan Chang, Yi Ding, Zhentao Shi, Bo Zhang

item.title: Propagation of Chaos in Contextual Flow Maps
item.description: arXiv:2605.16747v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We develop a quantitative statistical theory of transformers in the large-context regime by adopting the abstraction of contextual flow maps (CFMs): dynamical systems that evolve a distinguished token in the presence of a contextual measure across a stack of attention blocks. Within this framework, the finite-context model approximates an idealized infinite-context system in which the contextual measure is replaced by its underlying population, so that the context length $n$ becomes a statistical resource. Exploiting the McKean--Vlasov structure of the dynamics and the classical machinery of propagation of chaos, we establish a forward bound controlling the deviation between the finite- and infinite-context CFMs uniformly along depth, and a backward bound controlling the deviation between the corresponding training trajectories uniformly across iterations of online gradient descent. Both bounds achieve the optimal Wasserstein rate $n^{-1/d}$ for general CFMs and parametric rate $n^{-1/2}$ for a restricted class of CFMs that includes transformers as a special case. The analysis rests on a new Eulerian adjoint formulation of the loss gradient and stability estimates for the resulting forward--adjoint system, both of which may be of independent interest.
item.dc:creator: Shi Chen, Zhengjiang Lin, Kaizhao Liu, Philippe Rigollet

item.title: Functional Principal Component Analysis for Manifold-Indexed Data
item.description: arXiv:2606.31465v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Functional principal component analysis has traditionally focused on processes indexed by Euclidean domains, although functional observations increasingly arise on curved domains. We develop functional principal component analysis for real-valued processes observed at discrete locations on a general Riemannian manifold. We estimate the mean and covariance functions using intrinsic kernel smoothing based on geodesic distance and a normal-coordinate volume correction, with a general weighting scheme accommodating unequal numbers of observations across subjects. We establish $L^2$ and uniform convergence rates for these estimators and derive corresponding error bounds for the estimated eigenvalues and eigenfunctions. These results quantify how manifold dimension, sampling frequency and the weighting scheme affect estimation accuracy and characterize the phase transition between sparse and dense sampling regimes. Simulation studies on the circle and sphere, together with real-data applications, illustrate the finite-sample performance of the proposed methodology.
item.dc:creator: Chang Jun Im, Jeong Min Jeon

item.title: Kernel Ridge Regression over H\"older Classes: Function and Derivative Losses
item.description: arXiv:2607.26065v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We study ordinary kernel ridge regression over full H\"older-Zygmund balls, measuring errors in Sobolev norms and in pointwise and uniform losses for mixed derivatives. For targets of smoothness $s$, every RKHS norm equivalent to $H^{s+d/2}$ gives the optimal $H^r$ risk for $0\le r<s$; integer choices of $r$ include integrated squared derivative losses. Pointwise and uniform guarantees require additional kernel structure. A localized wavelet kernel attains the sharp derivative rates with the same regularization orders as for function estimation, whereas equivalent changes of the RKHS norm can destroy the population bias rates. For the ordinary Gaussian kernel with a shrinking bandwidth, we prove a uniform derivative risk bound with the optimal polynomial rate and an explicit, unoptimized logarithmic factor. The results allow bounded measurable design densities bounded away from zero and conditionally sub-Gaussian noise.
item.dc:creator: Yuxuan Hou, Yicheng Li

item.title: Minimax Rate for Diffusion-Guided Local Intrinsic Dimension Estimation based on Fokker-Planck Equation
item.description: arXiv:2609.04822v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Diffusion-guided methods have recently emerged as effective tools for probing the intrinsic geometry of high-dimensional data. Understanding their accuracy requires quantifying both (i) finite-scale approximation error relative to the true local intrinsic dimension (LID) and (ii) estimation error from finite samples. We address these two questions for the FLIPD field (Kamkari et al., 2024; arXiv:2406.03537), defined at the population level through the logarithmic scale derivative of a Gaussian-smoothed density and admitting a Fokker--Planck representation. For $\alpha$-smooth densities on a regular $d$-dimensional manifold, we establish a uniform $O(\sigma^2)$ approximation bound relative to the manifold dimension $d$. Under expected integrated squared loss, we prove a minimax lower bound of order $(n\sigma^d)^{-1}$ for estimating the FLIPD field from $n$ observations when $n^{-1/(2\alpha+d)}\le\sigma\le\sigma_0$. A plug-in FLIPD estimator based on the empirical denoising score matching (DSM) solution attains a matching upper bound. Thus the minimax rate is of order $(n\sigma^d)^{-1}$ and it becomes $n^{-2\alpha/(2\alpha+d)}$ at its smallest scale.
item.dc:creator: Jaehee Seo, Wontae Jeong, Jisu Kim

item.title: Nonparametric In-Context Learning under Growing Geometric Complexity: Minimax Optimality and Local Geometry-Adaptivity of Transformers
item.description: arXiv:2609.31458v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Transformers have become a central architecture for in-context learning (ICL), particularly through their state-of-the-art performance in large language models. This success motivates understanding how transformers exploit intrinsic geometry of real-world data. However, existing nonparametric ICL theory has largely focused on simplified settings, such as Euclidean domains or single manifold models, failing to fully explain its phenomenal empirical success in complex tasks. To address this gap, we study the prediction problem under unknown heterogeneous geometry, modeled by sample size-dependent mixtures of manifolds with heterogeneous dimensions, smoothness, and sampling masses. Under the growing geometric complexity model, we establish a minimax lower bound capturing the aggregate difficulty of the components and construct an oracle tangent local polynomial estimator with a matching upper bound. This estimator is connected to a structure-informed, two-stage softmax transformer with a geometric preconditioner and local polynomial solvers. The transformer achieves negligible approximation error relative to the minimax rate with logarithmic depth and polynomial size. Finally, we derive an in-context generalization bound for near empirical risk minimizers (ERM) over this class. Together, these results identify conditions under which the resulting predictor exploits local geometry and attains minimax rate.
item.dc:creator: Jaehee Seo, Jisu Kim

item.title: A Central Limit Theorem for Intrinsic Fr\'echet Means on Real Grassmannians
item.description: arXiv:2610.24159v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Subspace-valued data arise in dimension reduction, image-set and video recognition, and signal processing, and the Fr\'echet mean is their standard sample mean [12,10,16,24]. We establish a central limit theorem for the intrinsic sample Fr\'echet mean of i.i.d. observations on the real Grassmann manifold $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$, as a specialization of the general theorem of [19]. Unlike prior results which require the distribution to vanish or place negligible mass near the cut locus of the population mean, we allow a continuous, possibly positive density. To enable our results, we derive two properties of $\mathrm{Gr}(p,n)$: the first is that the union of the cut loci of all points within distance $\delta$ of the mean has volume $O(\delta)$. The second is that the Hessian of the squared distance function is integrable. We also give a smooth density on $\mathrm{Gr}(1,2)$ for which the mean is unique but the Fr\'echet Hessian vanishes.
item.dc:creator: Bipayan Banerjee, Imon Banerjee, Swagatam Das

item.title: On the Error Analysis of Triangular Transport Maps for Conditional Generation via MMD-based Objectives
item.description: arXiv:2610.33610v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Conditional generative models parameterized by triangular transport maps are widely used for conditional sampling, yet theoretical guarantees on the quality of the conditional measures they produce remain scarce. We address this question for minimum divergence estimators of triangular maps. We use MMD-based objectives as a tractable setting in which the gap between joint and conditional errors can be analyzed precisely, and we measure performance through the average conditional estimation error, defined as the squared maximum mean discrepancy (MMD) between the estimated and the true conditionals, averaged over the conditioning variable. We first show that the common practice of minimizing a joint MMD may fail to recover the conditionals: writing the joint and the conditional criteria as quadratic energies of the same conditional mean embedding residual, we prove that, for parametric classes, joint minimizers are generically inconsistent in the misspecified setting. We then analyze an estimator that directly minimizes the conditional criterion through a surrogate loss computable from joint target samples and reference samples. We prove a non-asymptotic error bound that decomposes the average conditional estimation error into approximation, estimation, and reference sampling errors, with fast rates independent of the ambient dimension in the parametric setting. Finally, for joint MMDs built from concentrating Gaussian kernels on the conditioning variable, we show that the joint criterion approximates a density-reweighted version of the conditional one, and we derive an error bound for the joint minimizer whose rate suffers from a curse of dimensionality in the conditioning variable. Our results suggest that training criteria for conditional generative models should target the conditional rather than the joint error, a principle that extends to other divergences and to dynamic transport.
